newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: FORECAST - Singapore Sept exports down 3.4 pct - poll.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Singapore Sept exports down 3.4 pct - poll.

text.p: Singapore's exports are continuing to suffer as a result of the worldwide slowdown in the electronics industry, a Reuters poll of economists suggested on Thursday.
Twelve leading financial institutions produced an average forecast of a fall of 3.4 percent year-on-year in nominal terms in the city-state's non-oil domestic exports.
This compares with a fall of 6.3 percent in August and a rise of 6.3 percent in July.
Forecasts for September ranged from a fall of seven percent to a rise of five percent year-on-year.
All economists polled said the recent poor export performance was due to a slump in demand for electronics and related components, on which Singapore is heavily dependent.
Electronics and related products account for about half the city-state's industrial production and almost 60 percent of its non-oil exports.
The same poll produced an average forecast of a 1.5 percent year-on-year rise in Singapore's consumer price index (CPI) of inflation. The CPI rose 1.4 percent year-on-year in August.
The government is expected to publish its official figures for exports and CPI for September in the next few days.
